title.orig: On the Origin of Species: the closing paragraphs
title.en: On the Origin of Species: the Closing Paragraphs

edition.en: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, first edition (London: John Murray, 1859), the last three paragraphs of chapter XIV, Recapitulation and Conclusion, as transcribed by Project Gutenberg (eBook 1228).
edition.zh: 据《论依据自然选择的物种起源》第一版（伦敦：约翰·默里，1859 年）第十四章“复述与结论”的最后三段，以古腾堡计划电子书第 1228 号为底本。

basis.en: Published in 1859; the author died in 1882.
basis.zh: 1859 年出版，作者卒于 1882 年。

note.en: After nearly five hundred pages of pigeons, barnacles, islands and fossils, Darwin steps back and looks at an ordinary entangled bank. The last sentence is one of the best-known in science, and this is its first-edition form; from the second edition on, Darwin added the words by the Creator after breathed. Notice how much of the passage looks forward, to psychology on a new foundation and to light on human origins, a subject the book otherwise leaves almost untouched.
note.zh: 在将近五百页的鸽子、藤壶、海岛和化石之后，达尔文退后一步，看着一处寻常的、草木纠缠的河岸。最后一句是科学史上最有名的句子之一，这里是它第一版的样子；从第二版起，达尔文在“注入”之后加上了“由造物主”几个字。请留意这几段有多少是在向前看：心理学将有新的基础，人类的起源将得到启明——而这个题目，全书别处几乎没有碰。

excerpt.orig: There is grandeur in this view of life, with its several powers, having been originally breathed into a few forms or into one; and that, whilst this planet has gone cycling on according to the fixed law of gravity, from so simple a beginning endless forms most beautiful and most wonderful have been, and are being, evolved.
excerpt.en: There is grandeur in this view of life, with its several powers, having been originally breathed into a few forms or into one; and that, whilst this planet has gone cycling on according to the fixed law of gravity, from so simple a beginning endless forms most beautiful and most wonderful have been, and are being, evolved.
excerpt.zh: 这种生命观是壮丽的：生命及其若干能力，最初被注入到少数几个类型或一个类型之中；而当这颗行星按照固定的引力法则不停运转的时候，最美丽、最奇妙的无穷无尽的类型，从如此简单的开端演化而来，并且仍在演化之中。
